key_insight: A variational derivation shows that gravity-based free-surface stabilization in incompressible Stokes flow is not just heuristic but emerges naturally from the weak form, along with an additional viscous boundary contribution.
engineering_relevance: This gives geodynamic solvers a firmer mathematical basis for stable free-surface simulation, helping reduce spurious oscillations without relying solely on ad hoc fixes.
method: Apply variational calculus to the energy-minimization form of incompressible Stokes flow.
Use the Gateaux derivative to derive the complete weak form for a deforming free-surface domain.
Identify boundary-integral terms from viscous deformation and gravitational body force.
evidence_signal: Two benchmark cases are used to verify that the derived formulation matches previously proposed stabilization approaches.
watch_item: The derivation is presented for the linear-viscosity case, so extensions to more complex rheology or implementation in existing solvers may require additional care.
paper_title: Variational Derivation of the Weak Form for Viscous Flows Involving Free Surfaces with Implications for Geodynamic Simulations
